### Interval Tree

[`IntervalTree`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html "Mutable interval tree over the projection of bounded shapes.") is a **mutable** one-dimensional index over bounded shapes. It
stores, for each shape, the closed interval its bounding box projects to on one
axis, and keeps the shapes themselves, so a query can go back to exact
two-dimensional geometry once the projection has pruned the candidates.

- `IntervalTree(shapes)` builds a tree over any iterable of bounded shapes, which
  may mix types; `IntervalTree()` starts empty. `IntervalTreeY` is the same class
  projecting on the y axis instead of on x.
- [`insert(shape)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#a2f8d70f5f499a90566d2bf2d3bc4bf54 "Inserts shape and its selected closed bounding-box interval.") and [`erase(shape)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#a5232163e9152216e4602bfee044b5940 "Removes one stored shape equal to shape.") add and remove one shape while keeping the
  tree balanced, so unlike a [`ShapeTree`](#shape-tree) it stays efficient after
  heavy mutation. Equal projected intervals are stored independently.

The queries come in two families, and they answer different questions.

The **projection** family decides from the intervals alone, never looking at the
shapes: [`countProjectionsIntersecting(query)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#a3e9f0fb15e803efb81b60a27bee3dadc "Counts shapes whose projected interval intersects the projection of q."),
[`reportProjectionsIntersecting(query)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#ae15ed226417c72c9acc097047b1e69eb "Returns copies of shapes whose projected interval intersects that of q."), [`emptyProjectionsIntersecting(query)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#a4efb73d10446f444b0accf4097530670 "Returns whether no stored projected interval intersects the projection of q."),
and the three `…ProjectionsContainedIn` counterparts. Touching at an endpoint
counts as meeting, and containment includes shared endpoints. Two shapes whose
x-ranges overlap may be nowhere near each other in the plane, so this is a
coarser question rather than a faster answer to the exact one.

The **exact** family prunes by the projection and then applies the
two-dimensional predicate: [`countIntersecting(query)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#a156229167292264d17c76144bb222538 "Counts stored shapes that geometrically intersect q."),
[`reportIntersecting(query)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#ab45e85ab0acaf3990602f9795873cf12 "Returns copies of stored shapes that geometrically intersect q."), [`emptyIntersecting(query)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#a8cd86feabd58f266e7339d8028c92b00 "Returns whether no stored shape geometrically intersects q.") and the three
`…ContainedIn` counterparts return exactly what a [`ShapeTree`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1ShapeTree.html "Static shape tree of bounded shapes.") returns over the
same stored shapes.

Every query is projected before anything else happens, so — unlike a
[`ShapeTree`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1ShapeTree.html "Static shape tree of bounded shapes."), which prunes the query against stored boxes — an unbounded shape is
rejected as a *query* as well as as an element.

Other methods: [`size()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#ac55a6eeebf7559e1f64933a9a9f45aae "Returns the number of stored shapes."), [`empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#ad88be49dab6c9f09d0d58e40a02df8a0 "Returns whether no shape is stored."), [`shapes()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#a4cb6798a11ec9ab0a74ef855e4d60c42 "Returns the stored shapes in internal storage order."), [`has(shape)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#ac311ca8d07c24b2f8edc96676aa72dfd "Returns whether a shape equal to shape is stored."), and the container
sugar `len(tree)`, `for shape in tree`, `shape in tree`.

- Other methods: [`countContainedIn`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#ae918a604763091e59b3c6652a4a3fc56 "Counts stored shapes geometrically contained in q."), [`countProjectionsContainedIn`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#ae7512c04c575239858fc93b464ccab27 "Counts shapes whose projected interval is contained in the projection of q."), [`emptyContainedIn`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#a5a39cac11c397647ef15094ac54c4c70 "Returns whether no stored shape is geometrically contained in q."), [`emptyProjectionsContainedIn`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#adc67523854627f68ef2c8c992943198e "Returns whether no stored projected interval is contained in that of q."), [`reportContainedIn`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#a139270ac2f3309e47b4015db43d3c30f "Returns copies of stored shapes geometrically contained in q."), [`reportProjectionsContainedIn`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1IntervalTree.html#adf6864ce62642b2afab0aa927ab18f6d "Returns copies of shapes whose projected interval is contained in that of q.").


### Arrangement

[`Arrangement`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html "The planar subdivision induced by a set of one-dimensional shapes.") is the subdivision of the plane induced by segments, rays and
lines. Its finite **vertices** are finite input endpoints, isolated input points,
crossings and the ends of overlaps; its **edges** are the atomic pieces between
them; and its **faces** are the connected components of the complement. Every
finite point of the plane belongs to exactly one cell.

Construction is exact and there is nothing to configure: two segments with
integer endpoints generally cross at a *rational* point, and coordinates here are
exact rationals, so every crossing is representable.

```python
a = pgl.Arrangement([pgl.Segment(0,0, 4,4), pgl.Segment(0,4, 4,0)])
a.vertexCount(), a.edgeCount(), a.faceCount()
# Output: (5, 4, 1)
```

- `Arrangement(shapes)` builds the arrangement of any iterable of shapes: points, segments and oriented segments, polylines and monotone chains, the boundaries of triangles, rectangles, convexes, polygons and regions, and lines, oriented lines and rays. The input may cross, overlap collinearly, repeat, share endpoints, or dangle with a free end; overlapping stretches are merged into one edge that remembers every shape covering it.
- `Arrangement(shapes, points)` additionally makes every given point a vertex wherever it falls: a point on a shape splits it there, and a point on nothing becomes a vertex incident to no edge, in the interior of the face holding it.

The structure is a doubly connected edge list, and the face of a halfedge is
always the one on its **left**, so a bounded face is enclosed by a
counterclockwise cycle and the outer boundary of a connected piece of the input
runs clockwise. All unbounded ends meet at one symbolic vertex at infinity,
ordered by their exact escape direction; there is no clipping frame, and every
halfedge really is part of some input shape.

Cells are named by three handle types — `VertexId`, `HalfedgeId` and `FaceId` —
which are distinct classes rather than plain integers, so a face handle cannot be
passed where a vertex handle is meant. Each has `index()` and `valid()`, and a
default-constructed one is the invalid handle.

- [`vertexCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a9bfe5b4cb80249fc1de127b50d919188 "Returns the number of finite vertices."), [`edgeCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a08f11793b25ddd2fb556024f743c0b5d "Returns the number of edges, i.e. half the number of halfedges."), [`halfedgeCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a6be0d6fc0290903229de2381a0d21e94 "Returns the number of halfedges: always even, twins being adjacent."), [`faceCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a51d90b5e5695c1ca8a8d8b6c661ff33c "Returns the number of faces, including every unbounded face."): the numbers of finite vertices, geometric edges, halfedges and faces, every unbounded face included. Face 0 is unbounded, though a line or a pair of rays can create several unbounded faces. The vertex at infinity is not counted, and its handle index is exactly [`vertexCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a9bfe5b4cb80249fc1de127b50d919188 "Returns the number of finite vertices.").
- [`vertices()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a2bb65a8786775e6483bcf31c977d19d9 "Returns the position of every finite vertex, in VertexId index order.") returns the finite vertices' positions, [`edges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a658e5933985b5519b6ff1bffe872182d "Returns every edge as a segment, line, or ray.") one [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label."), [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line.") or [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label.") per edge, and [`boundedEdges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a16442f32a0a800dde923998ad4a14b47 "Returns the bounded edges, omitting every ray and line.") only the segments.
- `position(v)` is a finite vertex's position — it raises for the vertex at infinity — and `halfedge(h)` is a halfedge's geometry, directed along it: an [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label."), an [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label.") or a [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label.").
- [`witness(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#af441a5410fccd05e29db0b5cc47bfe6f "Returns the vertex itself, as the witness of a zero-dimensional cell.") / [`witness(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#af441a5410fccd05e29db0b5cc47bfe6f "Returns the vertex itself, as the witness of a zero-dimensional cell.") / [`witness(f)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#af441a5410fccd05e29db0b5cc47bfe6f "Returns the vertex itself, as the witness of a zero-dimensional cell.") return a point of a cell: the vertex itself, a point inside an edge, and a point strictly inside a bounded face.
- Topology: [`twin(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#ae9cbf6c800e81f9844448c4955605400 "Returns the halfedge running along the same edge the other way."), [`next(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#ad26b2743252be523aaa112695da9229f "Returns the next halfedge along the boundary of the face on the left."), [`source(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a3e855a4641eb8f76ce19e455ec4f7d4f "Returns the vertex a halfedge leaves."), [`target(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#aac4567b70d33c495d2e73e7411826415 "Returns the vertex a halfedge arrives at."), [`face(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#ab0f9eb9a9380adc8e30e4d511c1d808b "Returns the face to the left of a halfedge."), [`outgoing(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#abc89a3616eccf001896fd74946214090 "Returns one halfedge leaving a vertex, or the invalid handle when the vertex is isolated."), [`outgoingHalfedges(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#ad388b90580685275b4259621a226c5f9 "Returns every halfedge leaving a vertex, in clockwise order.") (clockwise around a vertex, and accepting the infinity handle), and [`degree(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#abbf8bb0c7267ae2824a31bd6d4a8b8e5 "Returns the number of halfedges leaving a vertex.") — one halfedge per incident edge end, so a vertex where $k$ lines cross has degree $2k$.
- [`isUnbounded()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a4c561c065cadb4d7b36ef2c1b2fbe4f8 "Tells whether the arrangement contains an unbounded edge.") reports whether the arrangement has any unbounded edge; [`isUnbounded(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a4c561c065cadb4d7b36ef2c1b2fbe4f8 "Tells whether the arrangement contains an unbounded edge.") and [`isUnbounded(f)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a4c561c065cadb4d7b36ef2c1b2fbe4f8 "Tells whether the arrangement contains an unbounded edge.") ask about one edge or face, and [`isFictitious(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a5f478284cef3adb80cf2d2352f41619e "Tells whether a vertex is the symbolic point at infinity.") identifies the vertex at infinity.
- Faces: [`outerCycle(f)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a05069bcdb1916a1d21ba617d892285d9 "Returns a halfedge of the face's outer boundary cycle, which runs counterclockwise, or the invalid handle for an unbounded face."), [`innerCycles(f)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a074077c8678609fe02321d7865457327 "Returns one halfedge of each of the face's inner boundary cycles, each of which runs clockwise."), [`outerBoundaryOf(f)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#af8902ab9cdd64b29cb4ea514c780a0e9 "Returns the halfedges of a face's counterclockwise outer boundary."), [`innerBoundariesOf(f)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a6ce69c84e03c1a730b8e85e4a4fe4f60 "Returns the halfedges of every clockwise inner boundary cycle."), [`boundaryOf(f)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#ab6759442f288fc2db8514dddd87b59c3 "Returns every halfedge bounding a face, outer cycle first.") and [`hasSimpleBoundary(f)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a3224e1107d50043c33d7f6728b9dc979 "Tells whether a face's boundary is a single simple ring: no hole, and no edge with the face on both sides.").
- [`polygonWithHoles(f)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a205ae05e50d60caab291b28fc602c743 "Returns the closure of a bounded face as a region.") returns the closure of a bounded face as a [`PolygonWithHoles`](shapes.md#polygon-with-holes), regularized: a dangling edge sticking into the face is dropped, and a cycle pinching shut at a vertex is cut there into one ring per side. It raises for an unbounded face.
- [`halfplaneIntersection(f)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#aac2785cf3263014e41da06c326372616 "Returns the outer boundary constraints of a face as a half-plane intersection, ignoring holes.") returns the intersection of the supporting half-planes of the face's outer boundary, for a bounded or an unbounded face alike. It equals the face with its holes filled when that boundary is convex.
- [`label(cell)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a59a9ea3992f564c1797a1569afc1f17d "Returns the label an edge inherited from the input shape that produced it.") and `setLabel(cell, value)` read and write a [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.") label per edge or per face — what to use to record a classification per cell. [`originsOf(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a9297bbde7dbcd2b664e579112efb837b "Returns the positions, in the range the arrangement was built from, of every input shape that produced an edge.") and [`originsOf(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a9297bbde7dbcd2b664e579112efb837b "Returns the positions, in the range the arrangement was built from, of every input shape that produced an edge.") list the positions, in the input list, of every shape that produced a cell.
- Point location: [`locateFace(point)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a95d36d4248271458151cc640bf838704 "Returns the face containing a point.") returns the face containing a point (for a point on an edge or a vertex, the face an infinitesimal displacement lands in), and [`locateCell(point)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a20a88708be61b0431bf65e3b944b824a "Returns the vertex, edge, or face containing a point.") returns the cell that actually contains it, as a `VertexId`, a `HalfedgeId` or a `FaceId` — tell them apart with `isinstance`. [`buildPointLocation()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#af73b4d7888dfb82faaabaf0156b208a5 "Builds the randomized trapezoidal point-location index.") builds an exact trapezoidal map and search DAG, after which queries take expected logarithmic time instead of scanning the edges; [`hasPointLocation()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a0ffabaaa3d0a89074ae83a6b3a6f8321 "Tells whether locateFace currently uses the point-location index.") and [`clearPointLocation()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a7a17361bda2910fe462e306176dfc73f "Releases this arrangement's reference to its point-location index.") complete the trio.
- Tracing a directed curve: [`reportIntersecting(curve)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a1b4345f0c7e1facd1376e8a7c127b4c3 "Returns every vertex and edge met by a directed curve, in order.") returns the cells the curve meets, in order along it, [`firstIntersecting(curve)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a5862ce4aad1add7a6c1c3a40f664406b "Returns the first vertex or edge met by a directed curve.") only the first, and [`emptyIntersecting(curve)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a202256304a61715926954c0eb9e0d03c "Returns whether a directed curve meets no vertex or edge.") whether it meets none. The curve may be an [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label."), [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label."), [`MonotoneChain`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html "Weakly x-monotone polyline stored by lexicographically sorted vertices.") or [`Polyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html "Open polygonal chain stored in traversal order; may self-intersect."). Where the curve meets an edge only at one of its endpoints, the vertex there stands for the contact.
- [`asGraph()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html#a5c299514a909c3d750f9faff91d3e196 "Returns the vertex-edge incidence structure as a Graph.") returns the vertex-edge incidence structure as an `ArrangementGraph`, a [`Graph`](#graph) over vertex handles rather than points — the vertex at infinity has no position, so it could not be keyed by one.

A [Voronoi diagram](#triangulation) is an [`Arrangement`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Arrangement.html "The planar subdivision induced by a set of one-dimensional shapes.") whose faces carry their
generating site as a label, so the two share this whole interface.

- Other methods: `halfedge`, `position`, `setLabel`.


### Graph

[`Graph`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html "Undirected simple graph stored as adjacency sets.") is an undirected simple graph over points, the combinatorial companion of
the geometric structures: it is what the [visibility](algorithms.md#visibility)
methods return, and what `Triangulation.asGraph()` hands back.

- `Graph()` builds an empty graph, `Graph(edges)` one from a list of `(u, v)` endpoint pairs. [`addVertex(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#a24ad00aef263704a6de29e91790b002c "Adds a vertex if it is not already present.") adds an isolated vertex and [`addEdge(u, v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#ad16a529b19566b14e7f8c39ad15352c7 "Adds an undirected edge and its endpoints.") adds an edge along with any endpoint still missing; [`removeEdge(u, v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#ad995dddec014774cc4ab4d3350190c23 "Removes an undirected edge if it is present.") leaves the endpoints in place, [`removeVertex(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#a01dd69e09bf6d97010dc4b821fba0e68 "Removes a vertex and every incident edge.") deletes every incident edge with the vertex, and [`clear()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#ab3e3b01b7a1ce196c1cc6dbf9ab59c55 "Removes every vertex and edge.") empties the graph. A self-loop is ignored.
- [`containsVertex(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#a13af1a574d1154a8b648d267220bbd36 "Tests whether a vertex is present."), [`containsEdge(u, v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#ad761712593286f9ec5dcb24ebc8d601a "Tests whether an undirected edge is present."), [`vertexCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#a30d9b1889a6c6dbc67e2327a41c7772a "Returns the number of vertices."), [`edgeCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#ac91e80daafc93037fc43615c3b8cc97f "Returns the number of undirected edges."), [`maxDegree()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#afba58d8033ea13a134d53b4b5ef58c86 "Returns the largest vertex degree."), and [`degree(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#aa0e56dc340b090366e972cfd1b984511 "Returns the degree of a vertex.") — which returns `None` for an absent vertex.
- [`vertices()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#af171cf5f5b0b5a021afbffa7d3ffedaa "Returns a lazy view over the vertices."), [`edges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#ad05e39af26a52b0665de5125409ae9be "Returns a lazy view over the undirected edges."), [`neighbors(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#ab7d1d5987dba69f7c1ab020a6507f645 "Returns the neighbors of a vertex.") and [`closedNeighbors(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#ac7b11522a0d8be5669b71c3167430ab5 "Returns a vertex together with all of its neighbors.") return **sorted** lists, so a program's output never depends on hashing. [`edges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#ad05e39af26a52b0665de5125409ae9be "Returns a lazy view over the undirected edges.") gives each undirected edge once, as a `(u, v)` pair in increasing order. Asking about an absent vertex raises.
- [`bfs(v)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#a96aca939c3e4cc060cb72088a66326da "Traverses a connected component in breadth-first order.") returns the connected component of `v` in breadth-first order and [`bfs(v, k)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#a96aca939c3e4cc060cb72088a66326da "Traverses a connected component in breadth-first order.") stops after `k` vertices; [`components()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#a59f105712a9dbeda92cc0703c4a17fa3 "Returns the graph's connected components.") returns the connected components, largest first.
- [`biconnectedComponents()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#a7d824006e09e9f7780cfc28d38922a71 "Returns the vertex-biconnected blocks of the graph.") returns the vertex sets of the vertex-biconnected blocks, largest first: a bridge is a two-vertex block, an articulation vertex belongs to more than one, and an isolated vertex to none.
- [`cliqueCover()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#aa78575482ac3111a487f986b26eb27ba "Computes a vertex clique cover using the DSATUR heuristic.") partitions the vertices into cliques, largest first, by DSATUR coloring of the complement graph. The number of cliques is not guaranteed minimum.
- [`independentSet()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#a5741334841966ede109af18b88423ae3 "Computes a maximal independent set greedily from low-degree vertices.") returns a **sorted** maximal set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices, chosen greedily from the lowest-degree vertex up. Maximal, not maximum: every vertex left out is adjacent to one inside, but a larger independent set may exist. Vertices of equal degree are considered in an unspecified order, so which of several equally good sets comes back may vary between runs — only the ordering of the answer is fixed.
- [`spanningTree(weight)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#a6502db7f7bf67c808b5108926d5c5e1c "Computes a minimum spanning forest using Prim's algorithm.") returns a minimum spanning tree as another graph, by Prim's algorithm in $O(m \log m)$. `weight(u, v)` may return any comparable number — `Fraction` to stay exact, `float` for Euclidean lengths — and must be symmetric. A disconnected graph gives one tree per component, so the result always has the same vertices and components.
- [`shortestPath(source, target, weight)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#ab58eb2a3ec3b553dbecb29228beed1c5 "Computes a shortest path between two vertices using Dijkstra's algorithm.") returns the vertices of a shortest path, both ends included, by Dijkstra's algorithm. Weights must be non-negative and add up with `+`, neither of which is checked. A vertex to itself is that vertex alone, and an empty result means there is no path — different components, or an absent endpoint.
- [`shortestPath(source, target, weight, lowerBound)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1Graph.html#ab58eb2a3ec3b553dbecb29228beed1c5 "Computes a shortest path between two vertices using Dijkstra's algorithm.") finds the same path by A* instead: `lowerBound(v, target)` estimates what is left to travel and prioritizes the vertices that look closest, which expands far fewer of them than Dijkstra when the estimate is informative. It must be non-negative, must never exceed the true remaining distance and must be zero at the target — none of which is checked, and an overestimate simply returns a path that need not be shortest. It need not be consistent: a vertex is reopened whenever a shorter route to it turns up. Straight-line distance is the usual choice when the weights are Euclidean lengths.

```python
square = pgl.Polygon([0,0, 4,0, 4,4, 0,4])
graph = square.visibilityGraph()
tree = graph.spanningTree(lambda a, b: a.squaredDistance(b))   # exact weights
print(tree.edgeCount())
# Output: 3
```

A graph also behaves like a Python container: `len(graph)`, `for vertex in
graph` (sorted), and `vertex in graph`. It is mutable and therefore unhashable.


### Bit Matrix

[`BitMatrix`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html "A bit per cell of a rectangular window of the integer grid.") represents a digital geometry shape: the union of the unit squares $[x, x+1] \times [y, y+1]$ over a set of integer points, stored as one bit per cell of a rectangular window of the grid, packed into 64-bit words. Cell `(x, y)` is that unit square, named by its lower-left corner. The window is fixed at construction and never grows: writing outside it is a no-op and reading outside it gives `False`, so sizing it is the caller's job. It is the cheap representation for the rectilinear work an exact polygonal one makes expensive — the set algebra, the Minkowski operations, connectivity and morphology all run a word at a time — at the price of only representing what the grid can.

A matrix wears two hats, and which one an operation wears is in its name. As a **region of the plane**, the union of its cells as unit squares: that is what the predicates, [`area()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a3c53b00f19514108d8fb7637d9016e92 "Area the set cells cover, which is their number since each is a unit square."), [`perimeter()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#abeeae536951a380936b0af97051e6834 "Length of the boundary of the covered region."), [`centroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a0219f1379bc3d49b055595b2a76722cd "Centroid of the covered region."), [`bbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a0b64fc907fd6f793104bd0d1e5948122 "The rectangle the set cells cover, empty when no cell is set."), [`convexHull()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a4efbe98aa25a89fe9540e1ef00b6a718 "Convex hull of the covered region."), [`asPolygonWithHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a08e84dcab2b69587b87b9b93b4262fc5 "The covered region, as one region with holes."), [`asPolygonSet()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a893f8fda0b3434780b1066699ce3380f "The covered region, as a set of regions with holes."), the symmetries and [`minkowskiSum()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a1e05302ed563a514b7e95dc5e71c3801 "Returns the Minkowski sum of the two covered regions.") answer for, and they all commute with [`asPolygonSet()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a893f8fda0b3434780b1066699ce3380f "The covered region, as a set of regions with holes."). As a **set of lattice points**, each cell standing for its lower-left corner: that is what every [`lattice`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a6f8ad16cbdd5b18225fe55e74e85361a "The set cells as lattice points, in row-major order.")-prefixed operation works in, and it is the convention that makes a structuring element behave — a one-cell matrix is the identity of [`latticeMinkowskiSum`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a5aad41907198bb4ba24f24d2e1c1f244 "Returns the Minkowski sum {a + b : a in *this, b in other}.") and [`latticeMinkowskiErosion`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a517279210f2e0a91a0dc22696f0f8e2d "Returns the Minkowski erosion {p : p + other is inside *this}.") is its exact dual. The two readings differ by a cell: [`reflected()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a3e273ec3b92eda320bee9497bb67291f "Returns the reflection of the covered region through the origin.") maps cell `c` to `-c - (1,1)` where [`latticeReflected()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#ae1c3316550cad64df109c6537b015d69 "Returns the reflection of the cells as lattice points, {-c}.") maps it to `-c`. Translation reads the same either way.

A cell is named either by a pair of plain `int`s or by a [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload."), whichever reads better at the call site — [`m.set(3, 4)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a02f285b0627846151b9c0bb73243cb04 "Sets the cell; a cell outside the window is silently dropped.") and [`m.set(pgl.Point(3, 4))`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a02f285b0627846151b9c0bb73243cb04 "Sets the cell; a cell outside the window is silently dropped.") are the same call. A [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.") naming a cell must have whole coordinates: a fractional one raises rather than being rounded, since rounding it would move the cell.

- `BitMatrix(origin, width, height)` covers [`width`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a611a6de273ae5086246a8443b85c17d3 "Number of cells per row of the window.") by [`height`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a0b8f3400c92e441717de07745d3c8024 "Number of rows of the window.") cells from [`origin`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a8c45fa9e84583c97016863c1f541384c "Lower-left cell of the window."), all clear; a non-positive extent leaves the window empty. `BitMatrix(x, y, width, height)` spells the same thing with the origin as two ints. `BitMatrix(window)` takes the window as the [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners.") its cells cover, the inverse of [`window()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a449c49f6d8b37fcba70b0ef533d3434f "The window, as the rectangle its cells cover."). `BitMatrix(polygon)`, `BitMatrix(region)` and `BitMatrix(set)` rasterize a [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices."), a [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") or a [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.") whose every edge is axis-parallel, over its own bounding box, filling the cells it covers and leaving the holes and the gaps between components unset; each of those three shapes spells the same operation `asBitMatrix()`.

- [`innerRaster(shape, window)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/namespacepgl.html#aebdf56a5d5bef8597be76abfa4083561 "Rasterizes a shape into the cells it covers: its inner approximation.") and [`outerRaster(shape, window)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/namespacepgl.html#a9fe1fda9ac695d02fbb8f9ae220ca06d "Rasterizes a shape into the cells it meets: its outer approximation.") rasterize **any** shape, the first keeping the cells the shape contains and the second the cells it meets, so the two bracket the shape. Each costs one exact predicate per cell of the window, against the one pass per row a rectilinear region takes. The window may be left out, and is then the smallest cell window covering the shape's bounding box — which is why an unbounded shape ([`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label."), [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label."), [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line."), an unbounded [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.")) needs one given explicitly, though it rasterizes perfectly well once it has one.

- [`get(x, y)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#aeefec50cf74a081db467c9cb38d11d55 "Whether the cell is set; cells outside the window are not.") and [`set(x, y)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a02f285b0627846151b9c0bb73243cb04 "Sets the cell; a cell outside the window is silently dropped.") read and write one cell, along with [`set(x, y, value)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a02f285b0627846151b9c0bb73243cb04 "Sets the cell; a cell outside the window is silently dropped."), [`reset(x, y)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a9d6e9f472db235fb7186e617b6c50bb7 "Clears the cell; a cell outside the window is silently dropped."), [`flip(x, y)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a9348e83f65d7951625a377faf0550b3b "Flips the cell; a cell outside the window is silently dropped."), [`setAll()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a1d5c4a3754bd2703c3362bd406deab4e "Sets every cell of the window.") and [`clear()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a14fcf26073e1e3dc3e325aa3a73e425b "Clears every cell, keeping the window."). [`origin()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a8c45fa9e84583c97016863c1f541384c "Lower-left cell of the window."), [`width()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a611a6de273ae5086246a8443b85c17d3 "Number of cells per row of the window."), [`height()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a0b8f3400c92e441717de07745d3c8024 "Number of rows of the window."), [`window()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a449c49f6d8b37fcba70b0ef533d3434f "The window, as the rectangle its cells cover."), [`emptyWindow()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#af7b814ed95da25688a7667f18d51170e "Whether the window itself is degenerate, so no cell can be set."), [`inWindow(x, y)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a5b6b55752ddbc4e93795ddf72d18bd5f "Whether a cell is inside the window, and so can be set.") and [`sameWindow(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#acc9a0e1cdff6e1af2d44eca63e128c4c "Whether two matrices cover the same window.") describe the window; [`resized(window)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a5a51da3617ca50446c06fe6649f4828d "Returns the same cells over another window, dropping those outside.") moves the cells to another one, dropping those it cannot hold, and [`trimmed()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#add78a23cceee84ab85bca2969eca75ce "Returns the same cells over the smallest window holding them.") moves them to the smallest window holding them.

- [`count()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a10f9b141384b90dc37891849bfff9dd3 "Number of set cells.") and [`empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#abc76407568fdf5ebfe4269cbb1dd7fa3 "Whether no cell is set, which an empty window always is.") report the set cells. [`lattice()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a6f8ad16cbdd5b18225fe55e74e85361a "The set cells as lattice points, in row-major order.") returns them as [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.")s in row-major order and [`cells()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a9c95240f8c944e132c9820e137e9b8ec "The set cells as the unit squares they cover, in row-major order.") as the unit [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners.")s they cover; [`rectangles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#ae234d3aacbfaeb4a064e48511d698d68 "The covered region as maximal horizontal runs of cells.") instead merges each row's runs into as few disjoint covering rectangles as a row-major pass can, which is how to draw the cells as separate elements: `canvas.draw(matrix.rectangles())`.

- [`area()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a3c53b00f19514108d8fb7637d9016e92 "Area the set cells cover, which is their number since each is a unit square."), [`perimeter()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#abeeae536951a380936b0af97051e6834 "Length of the boundary of the covered region."), [`centroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a0219f1379bc3d49b055595b2a76722cd "Centroid of the covered region."), [`pointInside()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a29f58bb7f974461873d4a8dd74605188 "A point in the interior of the covered region.") and [`bbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a0b64fc907fd6f793104bd0d1e5948122 "The rectangle the set cells cover, empty when no cell is set.") measure the covered region: the number of cells, the length of its boundary counting the edges of a cell on the window border, the average of the cell centers, the center of the first set cell, and the rectangle the cells cover. All stay exact. [`centroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a0219f1379bc3d49b055595b2a76722cd "Centroid of the covered region.") and [`pointInside()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a29f58bb7f974461873d4a8dd74605188 "A point in the interior of the covered region.") raise when no cell is set. [`convexHull()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a4efbe98aa25a89fe9540e1ef00b6a718 "Convex hull of the covered region.") returns the hull of the region as a [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices.").

- [`asPolygonSet()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a893f8fda0b3434780b1066699ce3380f "The covered region, as a set of regions with holes.") returns the covered region as a [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors."), one component per edge-connected group of cells, so it has no precondition and keeps two components touching only at a corner apart. The boundary loops are read straight off the words, and vertices in the middle of a straight stretch are dropped along the way, so a filled box comes back as four corners however many cells it holds. [`asPolygonWithHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a08e84dcab2b69587b87b9b93b4262fc5 "The covered region, as one region with holes.") returns a single [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") and raises unless the cells form one edge-connected group, which a rasterized region and its Minkowski sums are. `canvas.draw(matrix)` draws the matrix as one element by drawing that polygon set.

- The shape predicates read the cells as the closed squares they are. [`contains(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#aa5a51f1bbf8199e990cb7dabf2971be9 "Whether the covered region contains the other one.") holds when every cell of `other` is a cell of this matrix, and [`interiorContains(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#aa5d30a313fa77b2b638cf31a16b36363 "Whether the interior of the covered region contains the other one.") when none of them touches the boundary either, corners included. [`intersects(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#ac9a3b9a294b12a9be150edc8c8d07139 "Whether the two covered regions share a point.") holds as soon as a cell of one comes within Chebyshev distance one of a cell of the other, since two cells sharing only an edge or a corner already share points; [`interiorsIntersect(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a2bd50da3d50ba3917ca335286023ccb1 "Whether the interiors of the two covered regions share a point.") is the stricter question of a shared cell. [`boundaryContains(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a137fcd49e5481b2cae97c6f2ad497db7 "Whether the boundary of the covered region contains the other one.") holds only for an empty `other`, a boundary being a curve and a nonempty matrix covering area.

- `&`, `|`, `^` and [`difference(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a3e70976cfce6150895b397905756d321 "The cells this matrix has and the other does not, over this window.") are the set algebra, with [`symmetricDifference(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a666f951d9cbc1f7c23868fcfa6b2dbe7 "The cells exactly one matrix has; the same as operator^.") spelling `^` out. Each returns the smallest window that provably loses no cell: the overlap of the two windows for an intersection, their hull for a union or a symmetric difference, the left window for a difference. The compound `&=`, `|=` and `^=` instead never move their window and drop whatever falls outside it, exactly as [`set`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a02f285b0627846151b9c0bb73243cb04 "Sets the cell; a cell outside the window is silently dropped.") does. [`andCount(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a97c3945a6d7634b8a797a808fab4a055 "Number of cells set in both matrices."), [`orCount(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#ad9fce0783604b3fe51d8f7433a5ccbc4 "Number of cells set in either matrix.") and [`xorCount(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a9678e7e29357c0051dc3ab297e086aae "Number of cells set in exactly one matrix.") give the three cardinalities without building the result. `~` is the complement *within the window*, not against the plane.

- The window is part of a matrix's value: `==` and the ordering compare it along with the cells, and the order is lexicographic on origin, width, height and bits, carrying no geometric meaning. [`samePointSet(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#af13ea0227a71ca82d61f8c2867b2a47c "Whether the two matrices cover the same region.") is the geometric question, and [`trimmed()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#add78a23cceee84ab85bca2969eca75ce "Returns the same cells over the smallest window holding them.") is the canonical form to compare by when only the region matters — a matrix is unequal to its trimmed form whenever trimming moves anything, while [`samePointSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#af13ea0227a71ca82d61f8c2867b2a47c "Whether the two matrices cover the same region.") always holds between them. Every window covering no cell has one canonical form, so all such matrices compare equal whatever origin they were built with. A matrix is mutable and therefore unhashable.

- [`translated(vector)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#ae9e8ec0e887c84581d7db635c7ddd318 "Returns the same cells translated by a vector.") moves the cells, spelled `matrix + point` or `point + matrix`, with `matrix - point` for the opposite and `+=` and `-=` in place. [`reflected()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a3e273ec3b92eda320bee9497bb67291f "Returns the reflection of the covered region through the origin.") (also `-matrix`), [`reflectedX()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a81030c515f2ed60887e618f2089091ca "Returns the reflection of the covered region across the x-axis."), [`reflectedY()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a5b2717e3aa7b1808be3d0e07e91328cc "Returns the reflection of the covered region across the y-axis."), [`transposed()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#abade5329c1e87d9db386632afe0a42b9 "Returns the reflection of the covered region across the diagonal."), [`rotated90(k)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a348554b430544eb9fc692de276c2a1dc "Returns the rotation of the covered region about the origin.") and its in-place [`rotate90(k)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a35fde5a565406b2d609a487e42f365da "Rotates the covered region about the origin.") are the symmetries of the covered region, so they commute with the conversion. The [`lattice`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a6f8ad16cbdd5b18225fe55e74e85361a "The set cells as lattice points, in row-major order.")-prefixed [`latticeReflected()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#ae1c3316550cad64df109c6537b015d69 "Returns the reflection of the cells as lattice points, {-c}."), [`latticeReflectedX()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a806f3908d0df113afaeb7965e362bf3f "Returns the reflection of the cells as lattice points, {(x, -y)}."), [`latticeReflectedY()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#adbb09939731761f973c26ab9f7803fbe "Returns the reflection of the cells as lattice points, {(-x, y)}."), [`latticeRotated90(k)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a6fe406b870d84a882669de77191e57fd "Returns the rotation of the cells as lattice points.") and [`latticeRotate90(k)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a91eb1ed2b845967bc01cc28df4481e6d "Rotates the cells as lattice points.") map the lattice points instead. Transposition is the exception the two readings agree on, so [`transposed()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#abade5329c1e87d9db386632afe0a42b9 "Returns the reflection of the covered region across the diagonal.") and [`latticeTransposed()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a1da956e44dca45f3b034430e2538306e "Returns {(y, x)}; the same as transposed, which the two readings agree on.") are the same operation.

- [`latticeMinkowskiSum(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a5aad41907198bb4ba24f24d2e1c1f244 "Returns the Minkowski sum {a + b : a in *this, b in other}.") is the sum of the two cell sets read as lattice points, over a window that is exactly the bounding box of the result. It costs one shifted or-assignment of the larger operand per cell of the smaller one, so a large region and a small structuring element are cheap. [`latticeMinkowskiErosion(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a517279210f2e0a91a0dc22696f0f8e2d "Returns the Minkowski erosion {p : p + other is inside *this}.") is its dual, the lattice points `p` with `p + other` inside this matrix, over this window shrunk by `other`'s bounding box; eroding by a matrix with no cell is vacuously true and fills the window. [`latticeOpening(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a6fd47894fc5b4765737dc6e3f2440adc "Returns the opening, a lattice erosion by other followed by a lattice sum.") and [`latticeClosing(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#ad753738bb3d9b128366d35518078400c "Returns the closing, a lattice sum with other followed by a lattice erosion.") compose the two in both orders.

- [`minkowskiSum(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a1e05302ed563a514b7e95dc5e71c3801 "Returns the Minkowski sum of the two covered regions."), also spelled `matrix + matrix`, is instead the sum of the two **regions**, so it commutes with the conversion. The unit square is not the identity of that sum — $U \oplus U$ is the two-by-two square — so this is the lattice sum dilated by the block that extra square covers, and comes out one cell wider and one cell taller in each direction. [`minkowskiErosion(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a4472c32611d2ea1d623fc29c10dfedbd "Returns the regularized Minkowski erosion of the covered regions.") is the region erosion, regularized the way a [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.") regularizes its own, which is what keeps it on the grid: a cell eroded by a cell is a single point, which has no area and is reported as empty.

- [`interior(adjacency)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a881a328302b4b1d22e0076d1569842f5 "Returns the set cells all of whose neighbors are set.") returns the set cells all of whose neighbors are set and [`boundary(adjacency)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#ad3494feeb3d894ad0cb498ba7d50e8c8 "Returns the set cells with at least one neighbor that is not set.") the rest of them, a cell on the window border always belonging to the boundary. `adjacency` is `GridAdjacency.edge` (4 neighbors) by default or `GridAdjacency.vertex` (8 neighbors).

- [`connectedComponents(adjacency)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#ab31cf82a65edf6230b56fd984a4c02b3 "Returns one matrix per connected group of cells, each trimmed.") returns one trimmed matrix per connected group of cells, [`componentCount(adjacency)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#aaf19389cda089b92c27b7ed602588375 "Number of connected groups of cells.") and [`isConnected(adjacency)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a4e377ed46b7e6b82bc333dfcf7ece9f4 "Whether the set cells form exactly one connected group.") count them, and [`fillHoles(adjacency)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a384ffa36e3ac1e487e72d7a12f51d8bd "Returns the cells together with every hole they enclose.") adds every group of unset cells that cannot reach outside. The background is always walked with the complementary adjacency, which is what keeps a diagonal chain of cells from both being connected and letting the background leak through it. [`holeCount(adjacency)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#ac37df5d6bc312680968d19af63bed551 "Number of holes the set cells enclose.") counts what [`fillHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a384ffa36e3ac1e487e72d7a12f51d8bd "Returns the cells together with every hole they enclose.") would add, and [`eulerNumber(adjacency)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a9ef04600ba0073fecee4cd4d062e3f41 "Euler characteristic of the covered region: components minus holes.") returns components minus holes.

- [`fillRows()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a1ba73c804a193ca86a9b68506e451922 "Fills the gaps of every row.") and [`fillColumns()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a1f3f1b3662e20e9aae0eef1810fcb81f "Fills the gaps of every column.") close the gaps of every row or column in place and report whether anything changed; [`makeHvConvex()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a54243f2a03dfcd9304d1c466d1c398e2 "Fills every cell that has set cells on both sides in its row and in its column, until nothing changes.") alternates them to a fixed point and returns how many cells it added, giving the smallest hv-convex superset. [`isRowConvex()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a5c00bb46ce4e9dd4363177b928701286 "Whether every row meets the set cells in a single interval."), [`isColumnConvex()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a8b03628e8e328bf94cca941956476e7b "Whether every column meets the set cells in a single interval.") and [`isHvConvex()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#a8b0ba86ecf5b1192bf9dcdc92b4faa96 "Whether every row and every column meets the cells in one interval.") ask whether that fixed point is already reached.

```python
room = pgl.Polygon([0,0, 10,0, 10,10, 0,10]).asBitMatrix()
robot = pgl.BitMatrix(0, 0, 2, 2)
robot.setAll()
free = room.minkowskiErosion(robot)          # where the robot's corner may sit
print(free.count(), free.isConnected(), free.asPolygonSet().componentCount())
# Output: 64 True 1
```

A matrix also behaves like a Python container: `len(matrix)` is the number of set cells, `for cell in matrix` yields them as [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.")s in row-major order, and `point in matrix` asks whether *that cell* is set — the question [`get`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/classpgl_1_1BitMatrix.html#aeefec50cf74a081db467c9cb38d11d55 "Whether the cell is set; cells outside the window are not.") answers, not whether the point lies in the covered region.
